title: Conditionals in CuTe DSL
key_concepts: Runtime conditionals are evaluated on the GPU
Compile-time conditionals use cutlass.const_expr and are evaluated during JIT compilation
Both branches exist in runtime conditionals, only the taken branch exists in compile-time conditionals
critical_patterns: Activation Functions: Use compile-time dispatch to eliminate runtime overhead
Precision Selection: Choose between FP16 and FP32 computations at compile-time
Bounds Checking: Use runtime conditionals for safe array access
Warp Divergence Mitigation: Use predicated execution to minimize divergence
constraints: Cannot use return, raise, or pass in dynamic conditionals
Variables defined in an if block are not available outside unless defined before
Cannot change variable types within conditionals
Runtime values cannot be used with cutlass.const_expr
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL provides support for conditionals in GPU kernels, distinguishing between runtime and compile-time conditionals. Runtime conditionals are evaluated on the GPU, with both branches existing in the generated code. Compile-time conditionals, using cutlass.const_expr, are evaluated during JIT compilation, resulting in only the taken branch being included in the generated code. Key patterns include activation functions, precision selection, bounds checking, and warp divergence mitigation. Activation functions can leverage compile-time dispatch to avoid runtime overhead, while precision selection allows choosing between FP16 and FP32 computations at compile-time. Runtime conditionals are useful for safe array access, ensuring bounds are checked during execution. Warp divergence can be mitigated by using predicated execution, reducing the performance impact of divergent threads. Constraints include the inability to use return, raise, or pass in dynamic conditionals, the need to define variables before conditionals if they are used outside, and the restriction against changing variable types within conditionals. Runtime values are incompatible with cutlass.const_expr, which is reserved for compile-time constants. Understanding these patterns and constraints is crucial for optimizing GPU kernel performance using CuTe DSL.
